# English → TOEFL Daily Lesson Cards (A0 → C2 Peak)

A complete **100-week** daily curriculum (600 day cards) from absolute beginner (A0) to **C2 / TOEFL iBT peak**, aligned to the **2026 TOEFL iBT format** (from 21 January 2026) in the later weeks.

## How to use

1. Open `COMPLETE-A0-to-C2-daily-lesson-cards.md` (or the stage file for your level).
2. Do **one card per study day** (Day 1–6). Rest on Day 7 or use it only for light Anki.
3. Keep a **portfolio folder**: voice memos, writing samples, error log, Anki exports.
4. Pass **gates** at Weeks 10, 22, 40, 58, 78, 100 before accelerating.

## Daily rhythm (~90–120 min)

| Block | Time | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| Warm-up | 10–15 min | Anki + activate + pronunciation |
| Learn | 25–35 min | Grammar point + concrete vocab + examples |
| Practice | 20–25 min | Controlled tasks |
| Produce | 20–25 min | Speak (voice memo) + Write (length target) |
| Review | 10–15 min | Anki cards for today + hardest sentence |

**Weekly load:** ~12 hours across 6 days. **Day 6** is heavier on review/integration.

## Stage map

| Weeks | Stage | File |
|------:|-------|------|
| 1–10 | A0→A1 | `01-a0-a1-weeks-01-10.md` |
| 11–22 | A2 | `02-a2-weeks-11-22.md` |
| 23–40 | B1 | `03-b1-weeks-23-40.md` |
| 41–58 | B2 | `04-b2-weeks-41-58.md` |
| 59–78 | C1 | `05-c1-weeks-59-78.md` |
| 79–100 | C2 / TOEFL peak | `06-c2-toefl-peak-weeks-79-100.md` |
| 101–110 | Optional stretch | see note in Week 100 / checklist |

## Resources (types — no required URLs)

- **Coursebook parallel:** any CEFR-leveled series unit matching the week grammar (A0–C1).
- **Anki / flashcards:** vocab + cloze grammar; tag `WeekW-DayD`.
- **Graded readers:** extensive reading 15–20 min on lighter days.
- **Pronunciation:** minimal pairs, shadowing, Listen and Repeat strings.
- **TOEFL (from ~Week 56 familiarization; serious from Week 71):** ETS Practice Test 1/2 and official-style materials for the **2026 iBT** task types only.
- **AWL:** Academic Word List for C1+ productive use (see checklist).

## 2026 TOEFL iBT task alignment (Week 71+)

**Do not practice retired formats** (old 4-task Speaking; Integrated/Independent essays).

- **Reading:** Complete the Words; Daily Life; Academic Passage
- **Listening:** Choose a Response; Conversation; Announcement; Academic Talk
- **Writing:** Build a Sentence; Email; Academic Discussion
- **Speaking:** Listen and Repeat; Interview

## Gates

See `07-master-checklist.md`. Rough rule: do not skip a gate week; collect evidence (recording + writing) and an honest yes/no.

## Scoring note (honest)

- TOEFL iBT section reporting uses a **1–6** band-style scale (not the legacy 0–120 total as your daily target number).
- **Peak phase target:** secure about **5.5** with stable timing and process, then **stretch toward 6**.
- Treating “120” as a casual synonym for perfection is fine motivationally, but pedagogically **band 6 is a stretch**.

# Stage 1 — A0 → A1 (Weeks 1–10)

Absolute beginner to elementary. Heavy phonics, be-verb, present simple, past of be, past simple regular. Pronunciation every week.

## Week 1 — Alphabet, sounds, greetings
**Level band:** A0/A1  
**Grammar focus:** be (I am / you are); alphabet & phonics  
**Weekly pronunciation:** integrate sounds/stress/linking in warm-ups; Day 6 includes a short pronunciation recycle.  
**Study load:** ~12 hrs/week across Days 1–6 (Day 6 = review/integration heavier).

### Week 1 · Day 1 — Alphabet & letter sounds
**Level:** A0/A1  
**Time:** ~90–120 min  
**Goal:** Learn and use 'be (I am / you are); alphabet & phonics' accurately while expanding vocabulary for 'Alphabet & letter sounds'.

**1. Warm-up (10–15 min)**  
- Re-read yesterday's checkpoint and mark yes/no honestly.
- Two-minute free speak on: 'Alphabet & letter sounds' (phone voice memo).
- Quick Anki: 10–15 due cards (new + review).
- Phonemes: shadow five minimal pairs or alphabet chant (day focus sound).

**2. Learn (25–35 min)**  
- Grammar/point: be (I am / you are); alphabet & phonics
- Pronunciation: focus on clear /iː/ vs /ɪ/, final -s, and word stress on new nouns.
- Vocab (10 items listed): one; two; three; four; five; six; seven; eight; nine; ten
- Examples (3–5 full sentences):
  - I am a student. I am two.
  - This is my one. It is new.
  - Are you from this city? Yes, I am. / No, I am not.
  - She is a teacher. He is an engineer.

**3. Practice (20–25 min)**  
- Controlled drill: ten gap-fills on (be (I am / you are); alphabet & phonics).
- Matching: match eight vocab items to definitions or pictures; then cover and recall.
- Sentence transformation: rewrite six sentences changing tense, aspect, or voice as required by today's point.
- Dictation: write four sentences from slow audio (self-record, then play back) focusing on today's forms.

**4. Produce (20–25 min)**  
- Speak: Record a voice memo on 'Alphabet & letter sounds'. Listen once and note three improvements. Target: 45–60 seconds; speak slowly with clear final consonants.
- Write: Write 4–6 sentences about 'Alphabet & letter sounds'. Check be/present forms. (about 40–60 words)

**5. Review (10–15 min)**  
- Anki: add today's new vocab (one, two, three, four, five, six…). Tags: Week1-Day1.
- Anki: grammar pattern card — one model sentence plus cloze deletion of the target form.
- Re-speak the hardest sentence from Produce until smooth (maximum three attempts).

**Checkpoint:** Without looking, write five vocab items plus three example sentences using today's grammar. Check accuracy. Pass if at least four vocab and two sentences are correct. Yes/No.

### Week 1 · Day 6 — Week 1 review & sounds
**Level:** A0/A1  
**Time:** ~90–120 min  
**Goal:** Integrate Week 1 skills on 'Week 1 review & sounds' and verify retention with mixed practice.

**1. Warm-up (10–15 min)**  
- Re-read yesterday's checkpoint and mark yes/no honestly.
- Two-minute free speak on: 'Week 1 review & sounds' (phone voice memo).
- Quick Anki: 10–15 due cards (new + review).
- Phonemes: shadow five minimal pairs or alphabet chant (day focus sound).

**2. Learn (25–35 min)**  
- Grammar/point: Spiral review — be (I am / you are); alphabet & phonics; error correction; recycling Week 1 vocab
- Pronunciation: focus on clear /iː/ vs /ɪ/, final -s, and word stress on new nouns.
- Vocab (12 items listed): one; two; three; four; five; six; seven; eight; nine; ten; mother; father
- Examples (3–5 full sentences):
  - I am a student. I am two.
  - This is my one. It is new.
  - Are you from this city? Yes, I am. / No, I am not.
  - She is a teacher. He is an engineer.

**3. Practice (20–25 min)**  
- Complete a mixed worksheet: 12–15 items covering this week's grammar (coursebook parallel or self-made).
- Listening: one graded audio (A0–B1) or short talk (B2+); write five detail notes.
- Transform drill: rewrite eight sentences from affirmative to question to negative.
- Partner or mirror: five-minute Q&A using only this week's structures.
- Error clinic: correct eight deliberate mistakes taken from your error log.

**4. Produce (20–25 min)**  
- Speak: Record a voice memo on 'Week 1 review & sounds'. Listen once and note three improvements. Target: 45–60 seconds; speak slowly with clear final consonants.
- Write: Write 4–6 sentences about 'Week 1 review & sounds'. Check be/present forms. (about 40–60 words)

**5. Review (10–15 min)**  
- Anki: add today's new vocab (one, two, three, four, five, six…). Tags: Week1-Day6.
- Anki: grammar pattern card — one model sentence plus cloze deletion of the target form.
- Re-speak the hardest sentence from Produce until smooth (maximum three attempts).
- Weekly deck filter: review all cards tagged this week; suspend leeches and rewrite them.

**Checkpoint:** Can you explain this week's main grammar in your own words and use it in five original sentences without notes? Yes/No.

**Time:** ~90–120 min  
**Goal:** Learn and use 'some/any/much/many/a lot of' accurately while expanding vocabulary for 'Count vs non-count'.

**1. Warm-up (10–15 min)**  
- Re-read yesterday's checkpoint and mark yes/no honestly.
- Two-minute free speak on: 'Count vs non-count' (phone voice memo).
- Quick Anki: 10–15 due cards (new + review).
- Pronunciation: one minute of word-stress tapping on today's new vocab.

**2. Learn (25–35 min)**  
- Grammar/point: some/any/much/many/a lot of
- Vocab (12 items listed): price; cheap; expensive; discount; receipt; cash; credit card; size; fit; try on; change; customer
- Examples (3–5 full sentences):
  - I went to the market and bought price and cheap.
  - This city is bigger and more expensive than my hometown.
  - We are going to travel next month if we get tickets.
  - I think it will rain later; look at those clouds.

**3. Practice (20–25 min)**  
- Controlled drill: ten gap-fills on (some/any/much/many/a lot of).
- Matching: match eight vocab items to definitions or pictures; then cover and recall.
- Sentence transformation: rewrite six sentences changing tense, aspect, or voice as required by today's point.
- Dictation: write four sentences from slow audio (self-record, then play back) focusing on today's forms.
- Cloze paragraph (80–120 words) targeting today's grammar and six vocab items.

**4. Produce (20–25 min)**  
- Speak: Record a voice memo on 'Count vs non-count'. Listen once and note three improvements. Target: 60–90 seconds; include five target vocab items and three target grammar forms.
- Write: Write 100–130 words on 'Count vs non-count'. Include connectors (and/but/because/so).

**5. Review (10–15 min)**  
- Anki: add today's new vocab (price, cheap, expensive, discount, receipt, cash…). Tags: Week13-Day1.
- Anki: grammar pattern card — one model sentence plus cloze deletion of the target form.
- Re-speak the hardest sentence from Produce until smooth (maximum three attempts).

**Checkpoint:** Without looking, write five vocab items plus three example sentences using today's grammar. Check accuracy. Pass if at least four vocab and two sentences are correct. Yes/No.

## Week 71 — TOEFL Reading Academic Passage (intro)
**Level band:** C1  
**Grammar focus:** 2026 Reading academic items  
**Weekly pronunciation:** integrate sounds/stress/linking in warm-ups; Day 6 includes a short pronunciation recycle.  
**Study load:** ~12 hrs/week across Days 1–6 (Day 6 = review/integration heavier).

### Week 71 · Day 1 — Passage mapping
**Level:** C1  
**Time:** ~110–120 min  
**Goal:** Learn and use '2026 Reading academic items' accurately while expanding vocabulary for 'Passage mapping'.

**1. Warm-up (10–15 min)**  
- Re-read yesterday's checkpoint and mark yes/no honestly.
- Two-minute free speak on: 'Passage mapping' (phone voice memo).
- Quick Anki: 10–15 due cards (new + review).
- Activate prior knowledge: list five words you already know related to today's topic.
- TOEFL micro: three to five warm items matching today's skill focus (unofficial practice acceptable).

**2. Learn (25–35 min)**  
- Grammar/point: 2026 Reading academic items
- TOEFL alignment: practice must map to current iBT tasks (Reading: Complete the Words / Daily Life / Academic Passage; Listening: Choose a Response / Conversation / Announcement / Academic Talk; Writing: Build a Sentence / Email / Academic Discussion; Speaking: Listen and Repeat / Interview).
- Vocab (14 items listed): choose a response; conversation; announcement; academic talk; gist; attitude; function; connecting content; note-taking; campus; lecture; paraphrase; build a sentence; email
- Examples (3–5 full sentences):
  - The announcement primarily functions to notify students of a schedule change.
  - Complete the Words items often hinge on morphology and collocational expectancy.
  - A strong Interview answer organizes idea, reason, concrete example, then close.
  - Hedging (for example, appears to) is appropriate when evidence is limited.

**3. Practice (20–25 min)**  
- Controlled drill: ten gap-fills on (2026 Reading academic items).
- Matching: match eight vocab items to definitions or pictures; then cover and recall.
- Sentence transformation: rewrite six sentences changing tense, aspect, or voice as required by today's point.
- Dictation: write four sentences from slow audio (self-record, then play back) focusing on today's forms.
- Cloze paragraph (80–120 words) targeting today's grammar and six vocab items.
- Timed accuracy set: eight items in six minutes; mark and classify errors (form vs meaning).
- Paraphrase set: rewrite five sentences preserving meaning with denser or more academic wording.
- TOEFL-aligned micro-set: 6–10 items of the day's target task type; review explanations.

**4. Produce (20–25 min)**  
- Speak: TOEFL Speaking practice: Listen and Repeat (8–12 strings) plus Interview (four questions). Voice-memo everything; self-score intelligibility 1–6.
- Write: TOEFL Writing triad light: five Build-a-Sentence items plus one Email plus one Academic Discussion (timed). Revise Discussion once.

**5. Review (10–15 min)**  
- Anki: add today's new vocab (choose a response, conversation, announcement, academic talk, gist, attitude…). Tags: Week71-Day1.
- Anki: grammar pattern card — one model sentence plus cloze deletion of the target form.
- Re-speak the hardest sentence from Produce until smooth (maximum three attempts).
- AWL note: if any Academic Word List item appeared, mark productive (used in speak/write) vs receptive.

**Checkpoint:** Did you complete today's TOEFL-aligned micro-set and write one process note (what slowed you down)? Yes/No.

# Stage 6 — C2 / TOEFL Peak (Weeks 79–100)

Peak training on current TOEFL iBT (2026) sections. Secure ~5.5 then stretch toward 6. Full section sims and two mixed simulations. Week 100 taper. Optional Weeks 101–110 stretch noted briefly.

## Optional stretch — Weeks 101–110 (overview only)

These weeks are **not** full daily cards. If you have completed Week 100 and still need polish:

| Week | Focus |
|-----:|-------|
| 101–102 | Reading leaks (Complete the Words, Academic Passage) |
| 103–104 | Listening endurance (Conversation, Academic Talk) |
| 105–106 | Writing triad precision |
| 107–108 | Speaking (Listen and Repeat + Interview) |
| 109 | Mixed light simulation |
| 110 | Final taper |

Keep the same daily rhythm if you wish, but recycle Week 79–100 templates with fresh official-style items. No new CEFR grammar syllabus.

# Master Checklist — Gates, AWL, Resources

## Progression gates (must collect evidence)

### Gate A1 — Week 10
- [ ] Introduce yourself and describe daily routine (60–90 sec voice memo)
- [ ] Write 60–80 words in present + past (regular) with ≤3 major errors
- [ ] Recognize 300+ high-frequency words receptively
- [ ] Checkpoint Days 5–6 marked Yes

### Gate A2 — Week 22
- [ ] 90–120 sec talk: past trip + future plan + advice
- [ ] Write 120–150 words using connectors and present perfect at least once
- [ ] Can use going to / will / should / first conditional in speech
- [ ] Portfolio samples saved

### Gate B1 — Week 40
- [ ] 2–3 min monologue with discourse markers
- [ ] Write 180 words: clear paragraph structure
- [ ] Follow a short academic-style paragraph and summarize orally
- [ ] Listening: gist + 5 details from one recording

### Gate B2 — Week 58
- [ ] 3–4 min interview answers with hedges and examples
- [ ] Write 220–250 words semi-formal OR email + discussion sample
- [ ] Read a long article and give oral précis
- [ ] Light TOEFL familiarization complete (no full test required)

### Gate C1 — Week 78
- [ ] Academic Discussion + Email timed samples meet task fulfillment
- [ ] Listen and Repeat intelligibility self-score ≥5 on familiar strings
- [ ] Interview answers organized and concrete
- [ ] Diagnostic across 2026 task types logged
- [ ] Honest plan: secure 5.5 then stretch to 6

### Gate C2 / Peak — Week 100
- [ ] Two full-section simulation cycles reviewed (Practice Test style)
- [ ] Top leaks closed or consciously managed
- [ ] Test-day logistics script written
- [ ] Taper completed (no heavy cramming Day 6 Week 100)

## AWL note

From **Week 60**, treat Academic Word List items as **productive** targets:
- Add to Anki with collocations (not translations alone).
- Force use in Academic Discussion and oral summaries.
- Track receptive → productive upgrades weekly.

## Resource list (types)

| Type | Use |
|------|-----|
| CEFR coursebook | Parallel grammar/vocab to each week |
| Anki | Daily SRS; tags WeekW-DayD |
| Graded readers | Fluency & vocab recycling |
| Dictionary (EN–EN) | From B1 onward |
| Pronunciation drills | Minimal pairs; shadowing; L&R |
| ETS Practice Test 1/2 | Peak simulations (2026 format) |
| Error log (spreadsheet) | Form / meaning / pronunciation / timing |
| Portfolio folder | Writings + voice memos + gate artifacts |

## Optional stretch — Weeks 101–110 (brief; not full daily cards)

Use only if post-100 scores need polish:

- **101–102:** Reading leaks only (Complete the Words + Academic Passage).
- **103–104:** Listening endurance (Conversation + Academic Talk).
- **105–106:** Writing triad precision (zero careless errors).
- **107–108:** Speaking intelligibility + Interview density.
- **109:** Mixed light simulation.
- **110:** Final taper + exam.

Do **not** add new grammar systems; only stabilize process and timing.

## Weekly self-audit (every Day 6)

- [ ] 6 day cards completed this week
- [ ] Anki due ≤ backlog of 1 day
- [ ] At least 4 voice memos saved
- [ ] At least 4 writing samples saved
- [ ] Top 3 errors identified for next week
